upper_row_ss: "wherein the grating coupler comprises a first grating region and a second grating region, the first grating region configured to couple a first polarization component of the input optical signal and the second grating region configured to couple a second polarization component of the input optical signal, the first and second polarization components being orthogonal;"

The grating coupler structures in both accused products comprise two distinct grating regions, each configured to couple a different orthogonal polarization component of the input optical signal. LumiLink 800G-DR8: The Benchmark teardown identifies two distinct grating regions within the coupler structure of the LumiLink 800G-DR8. The first grating region is configured to couple the TE polarization component of the input optical signal, and the second grating region is configured to couple the TM polarization component into a separate waveguide channel. These regions are clearly delineated in the annotated SEM images provided in the teardown report. [Benchmark-800G-DR8-020, Fig. 9 (annotated top-down SEM with region boundaries marked, showing Region A (TE coupling) and Region B (TM coupling).] The two regions exhibit distinct grating parameters (pitch, duty cycle, and orientation) consistent with coupling different polarization states, as measured by Benchmark's metrology analysis. LumiEdge 1600G-LR: An analogous dual-region grating coupler architecture is observed in the LumiEdge 1600G-LR, with the same fundamental design approach of dedicating separate grating regions to each polarization component. [Benchmark-1600G-LR-016, Fig. 8 (annotated top-down SEM with analogous region identification).] Orthogonality: TE (transverse electric) and TM (transverse magnetic) modes are orthogonal polarization states by definition in the field of optics and photonics. A person of ordinary skill in the art would understand the TE and TM modes coupled by the grating regions in the accused products to constitute "orthogonal" polarization components within the meaning of this claim limitation. Lumincore Design Documentation: Lumincore's internal photonic design rule document for the accused products explicitly describes the grating coupler as having "separate coupling regions for each polarization axis." [LTC-PROD-049115, p. 14 ("The grating coupler architecture employs separate coupling regions for each polarization axis, with Region 1 optimized for TE-mode coupling and Region 2
lower_row_ss: optimized for TM-mode coupling.")..] This document further specifies that the two regions are designed with different grating parameters to achieve efficient coupling for each respective polarization mode, confirming that the accused products embody this claim limitation.

upper_row_ss: "The silicon photonic transceiver module of claim 1, further comprising a polarization rotator element disposed on the photonic integrated circuit, the polarization rotator element configured to rotate the polarization of one of the first polarization component or the second polarization component such that both the first polarization component and the second polarization component propagate in a same polarization mode in their respective waveguides."

Both accused products include a polarization rotator element disposed on the photonic integrated circuit that rotates the polarization of the TM-mode component into the TE mode after coupling by the grating coupler, so that both waveguide paths carry TE-mode signals for downstream coherent processing. This is a standard and well-known design approach in polarization-diverse receiver architectures in silicon photonic systems, where downstream optical components (e.g., optical hybrids, photodetectors) are typically optimized for TE-mode operation.Benchmark Teardown Evidence:The Benchmark teardown identifies a dedicated polarization rotator structure on the PIC of both accused products, located downstream of the second waveguide output of the grating coupler (i.e., the waveguide carrying the TM-mode component). [Benchmark-800G-DR8-025, Fig. 14 (SEM image of polarization rotator structure on LumiLink 800G-DR8 PIC, annotated with dimensional measurements); Benchmark-1600G-LR-019, Fig. 11 (analogous SEM image of polarization rotator structure on LumiEdge 1600G-LR PIC).] The polarization rotator in both products is a mode-evolution-based rotator, which gradually converts the TM0 mode to the TE0 mode over a tapered waveguide section, as confirmed by the physical geometry observed in the teardown.Lumicore Design Documentation:Lumicore's design documentation explicitly describes the presence and function of the polarization rotator element. [LTC-PROD-049301, at 7 ("Following the grating coupler's TM output waveguide, a TM-to-TE polarization rotation stage converts the coupled TM-mode signal into TE-mode for compatibility with the downstream coherent receiver optical hybrid, which operates in TE mode.").] This document further specifies the design parameters of the rotator, including its length, taper geometry, and target extinction ratio for polarization conversion.
lower_row_ss: Deposition Testimony: Kevin Ng of Benchmark confirmed in his deposition that the teardown analysis revealed a dedicated polarization rotator element downstream of the grating coupler's second waveguide output in both accused products. [Ng Dep. Tr. at 45:10-46:3 ("Q: Did you identify a polarization rotator element in the LumiLink 800G-DR8? A: Yes, we did. It was located immediately downstream of the grating coupler's second output waveguide — the one we identified as carrying the TM-mode signal. Q: And what does the polarization rotator do? A: It converts the TM-polarized light into TE-polarized light, so that both channels are in the same polarization mode for the rest of the chip."). Dr. Michaud's deposition testimony further confirmed the design intent behind the polarization rotator: [Michaud Dep. Tr. at 115:3-116:1 ("Our coherent receiver architecture requires both signal paths to be in TE mode before they reach the optical hybrids. The polarization rotator on the TM path handles that conversion.").].
